question: What is the recommended first-line pharmacological treatment for generalised anxiety disorder (GAD) requiring long-term management?

answers.text: SSRI or SNRI (e.g., escitalopram, venlafaxine) — effective for chronic anxiety, no dependence liability, concurrent antidepressant effect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. SSRIs and SNRIs address the underlying serotonergic dysregulation in the amygdala-prefrontal fear circuit. They are effective long-term without tolerance or dependence, and treat comorbid depression (present in ~60% of GAD patients). Their delayed onset (4–6 weeks) means short-term BZD bridging may be needed initially.

answers.text: Long-term diazepam — most effective anxiolytic with decades of evidence for GAD

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Benzodiazepines are highly effective short-term (≤4 weeks) but cause tolerance, physical dependence, cognitive impairment, and fall risk with long-term use. After 4–6 weeks, the patient often needs escalating doses and experiences inter-dose rebound anxiety — creating iatrogenic dependence.

answers.text: Alprazolam — high-potency BZD proven most effective in GAD long-term trials

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Alprazolam is a short-acting, high-potency BZD with particularly high dependence liability and severe inter-dose rebound anxiety. It is one of the most difficult BZDs to discontinue. International guidelines explicitly recommend against long-term alprazolam for GAD.

answers.text: Hydroxyzine — safest anxiolytic with no dependence risk and immediate onset

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hydroxyzine (H₁ antihistamine) has mild anxiolytic properties and no dependence risk, but its efficacy for chronic GAD is limited compared to SSRIs/SNRIs. It is suitable for situational/pre-operative anxiety, not as first-line maintenance for GAD.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key principle: benzodiazepines are effective but cause tolerance and dependence with chronic use (>4 weeks). SSRIs/SNRIs are first-line for all chronic anxiety disorders because they address underlying pathophysiology without dependence risk.

The general goal of anxiety pharmacotherapy: BZDs for short-term relief (≤4 weeks) or as a bridge during SSRI initiation; SSRIs/SNRIs for long-term management. This distinction prevents the common clinical error of prescribing indefinite BZDs.
